body: Seems like this special case is specific to react. Maybe we should remove this special case logic from `no-undef` or at least make it an opt-in option.

It's tricky to say, the only other JSX compilers I could find were https://www.npmjs.com/package/virtual-dom-jsx and https://github.com/insin/msx

Their examples all show using lowercase strings, and from reading their implementations they appear to follow React's rules about strings vs variables.

This is definitely a bug as it behaves today. The real question is the solution. 

I could see an argument for removing the current exceptions altogether, as this seems to be a React - specific set of semantics (which is why we are in this situation in the first place). But to remove it, we would need to expose something so plugins could implement this same functionality.

The decision to support JSX at all was a pragmatic one, I think treating React's approach to variable vs strings for "tag names" as the official approach is in-line with that choice (while supporting the `React.createElement` stuff is a step too far as already discussed).

I suspect if the existing JSX semantic knowledge is removed from these rules it will generate quite a lot more queries from users :(

issue.title: Consider including difference between <tag> and <Component> in spec

repository.name: jsx
repository.description: The JSX specification is a XML-like syntax extension to ECMAScript.

issue.body:
This arose in relation to https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/1911

Currently, the spec has a single node type for JSXElementName, which separates three cases: identifier, xml-namespaced identifier, JS member expression identifier.

In the implementation as of 0.12, the semantics of a tag differ depending on the casing of the first character of the identifier.

Could this be incorporated in some way? Perhaps as `JSXComponent` vs `JSXIdentifier` or `JSXIdentifier` vs `JSXTag`. Something to indicate that one should be interpreted as a variable reference, and one as a string literal.

body:
I'm not sure if it was pragmatic or just misinformed. The fact that semantics have changed means we likely made the wrong choice. We can't be caught in a situation where the core rules are at the mercy of a library defining what the semantics of some syntax is.

So I think the right way forward here is to remove the exception and add a way for doors to mark a variable as used. Then we can work with @yannickcr to make sure eslint-plugin-react is updated to make up for this change.

Would that just be a case of making https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/7bb738f67fbe441e8769134ede1a46431614c1dc/lib/rules/no-unused-vars.js#L102 an officially documented thing?

I should be able to extend the stuff i did in yannickcr/eslint-plugin-react#6 to make that work.

Would you also want to remove the JSX variable support from `no-undef` ?
I am open to update eslint-plugin-react to handle these cases, but, as you said, we need a way to mark a variable as used (or to remove a reported error ?)

How about something along these lines? Using the shared settings feature to ensure the rules are using the same flag on AST nodes to flag usage.

https://github.com/glenjamin/eslint/commit/d779288e694be5ea929f157ea6617276c52df791
I'd like something that is a method call. Relying on people finding the variable and setting a property is too error prone.
Would that be something exposed on RuleContext? It does seem a bit too one-rule-specific to live there, but I'm not familar enough with the internals to suggest anywhere better.
Yeah, probably RuleContext. We only have one documented use case for it right now, but I could easily see other rules wanting to say something was used.

I think that's the idea, but we don't want people searching through the scope to find nodes. Ideally we would have something like:

``` js
context.markVariableAsUsed("foo");
```

And it would search from the current scope to find that identifier and mark it as used. That way, rules wouldn't need to worry about scoping to make this work.

Here's another draft: should I be using a PR for WIP stuff? https://github.com/glenjamin/eslint/commit/aa7367c

There's currently no tests for `rule-context.js`, presumably because it's implicitly tested via all the rule tests? Once the JSX variable handling is removed from core then nothing will be using the new function - is there a way to create an anonymous rule or something similar to test this new API? If not i guess I'll have to do some similar bootstrapping to what eslint-tester does to get an AST I can test against?

The functionality should live on the `eslint` object and be exposed on `RuleContext`. That's how most of the methods work. Then you can write a test using `eslint` (plenty of examples in the test file).

issue.body:
I've not raised a separate issue, as it took me as long to make the patch as it would to raise an issue in the first place (and I read the contributing docs a bit late!) - this is somewhat related to https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/1905

React is in the process of removing the tag whitelist in JSX - it's slated to land in React 0.13 (https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/2746)

The current rule is that JSX tags beginning with a lowercase character will transform to a string, and others will transform to a variable.

This logic already exists in the `no-undef` rule, this patch includes the same logic in `no-unused-vars`.

body:
Ok, latest WIP is pushed to glenjamin/eslint@852be6d

I'm not really happy with my approach for testing that the `no-unused-vars` rule can be influenced by calling `markVariableAsUsed`, but I can't see another way to run a custom rule alongside a core rule.

Any suggestions?
I think that's fine. Can you for a PR? I think we are close on this.
